newsitem.title: UK: Granada says hotel sales on track.
newsitem.headline: Granada says hotel sales on track.

text.p: British media and leisure company Granada Group Plc said on Monday it was happy with the progress it was making on the sale of its Exclusive hotels.
"We are quite confident the disposals are on track...We are very happy with the way the sales process is progressing," said a Granada spokesman.

Granada shares weakened on Monday on fears that the company may fail to match the 800 million stg book price on the sale of the remaining 16 Exclusive hotels it acquired in its 3.9 billion stg takeover of Forte last January. Granada shares were 4p lower at 878p at 1600 GMT.
Granada last week sold London's Hyde Park Hotel to Mandarin Oriental International for 86 million stg, a gain on book value of some 15 million stg.

The Financial Times reported on Monday that Granada may decide to keep hold of its flagship Grosvenor House Hotel in London if offers for it fall far below the 350 million stg it is reported to be seeking. The Granada spokesman declined to comment on specific hotels. The newspaper said that property company Chelsfield Plc was set to buy the Westbury Hotel in London's West End. The property has a book value of 33 million stg.

A report in the Sunday Times said that a consortium of Irish investors led by Dermot Desmond was close to buying the Sandy Lane hotel in Barbados at a price of 40 million stg. The book value is 26.6 million stg.
Granada chairman Gerry Robinson said last week that he expected the hotel sales process to be completed by early 1997.
